title: Signs for those who think
hookLine: in the heavens and earth and the turning of night and day are signs (Quran 3:190)

cards: Late at night, a man gets up from his bed and looks at the sky.

A report in the hadith collection of al-Bukhari tells it this way: Ibn Abbas was staying in the house, and saw the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, wake in the night, look up at the heavens, and recite the closing verses of the Qur'an's third chapter.
Those verses begin with the sky, and with the plain fact that night turns into day. Here, awe and thinking go together.

teach.b: In paraphrase, Surah Al Imran says: in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, there are signs for people of understanding.
Nothing exotic: sky, ground, and the fact that it gets dark and then light again. Second, the word signs. In Arabic it's ayat.

A sign points past itself, the way a road sign isn't the city but tells you the city is there. In Islamic teaching the world is full of these pointers, and Muslims use the same word, ayat, for the Qur'an's own verses.
The book has signs, and so does the sky. Third, who sees them. The verse doesn't say signs for everyone.
It says signs for people of understanding.
The next verse describes them: people who remember God standing, sitting and lying down, who reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and say: our Lord, you did not create this in vain.
Remembering and thinking, together. Awe, here, isn't the end of thought. It's where thought goes when it follows something all the way.
Fourth, what it asks of an ordinary day. The turning of night and day happens whether anyone notices or not.
The verse asks for noticing, and then for a question: what is this pointing to?
For Muslims, the answer is God. For anyone, the turning of the day is still there to watch, and to think about.

how: Muslims recite the closing verses of Surah Al Imran, and some recite them on waking in the night, following the report that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ did; reflection on creation is called tafakkur.

games.why: for people of understanding: those who remember God standing, sitting and lying down, and reflect on creation.

practice: Find the light where you are, a window, a doorway, the way it falls across the room, and tell the time of day by the light alone: high and white, low and gold, gray, or electric, and which way the shadows lean.
Then ask one quiet question, and don't rush it: what is this pointing to? If you pray, you can remember God as you sit, as the verse describes; if not, let the question stay open.

wordCard.voice: Ayat. The Qur'an's word for signs, pointing past themselves in the sky, the earth and the turning of night and day, for people who reflect. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: signs. also the word for the verses of the Qur'an.
